findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plain text in the Lambda function's environment variables, readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration and committed to version control.
The Lambda environment variables are not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key (no kms_key_arn set), so sensitive values rely only on the service default key and are exposed in the console/API.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is deprecated and no longer receives security patches from AWS.
No vpc_config is defined, so the function runs outside a VPC with unrestricted network egress and no security group/subnet-level traffic control, providing an exfiltration path.

The Lambda execution role has no permissions boundary and no explicit least-privilege policy attached, so any policy later attached to it is unconstrained; the trust policy also lacks source account/ARN conditions.
